output.proposal: HB No. 11768 seeks to modernize and reorganize the Bureau of Immigration by redefining its powers and functions, professionalizing its organization, upgrading the compensation and benefits of its officials and employees, and replacing the Philippine Immigration Act of 1940 and the Alien Registration Act of 1950 with a single updated immigration law. It also creates an Immigration Trust Fund sourced from a share of immigration collections to finance modernization, benefits and training.
output.alignment: As a government organization measure that reorganizes an existing bureau rather than creating a new body, the review should examine the proposed governance structure of a Board of Commissioners and up to five Boards of Special Inquiry (Sections 5 and 14), the new divisions and operating offices (Section 19), and the creation, reclassification and upgrading of positions (Section 116), and assess whether these are consistent with the streamlining and reorganization intent of the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). The review should also assess the earmarking of thirty percent of immigration collections for the Immigration Trust Fund (Section 118) against general fund and budget practice. No priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework has been identified for the measure. It corresponds to item 43 of the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda, Modernizing the Bureau of Immigration.
legislative_history: HB No. 11768 was filed on October 29, 2026 by Representative Marlyn L. Primicias-Agabas; later stages are not yet on record.
HB No. 9801 of the 20th Congress carries near-identical text under the short title Immigration Modernization Act.

Bills with matching titles on modernizing the Bureau of Immigration were filed earlier in the 20th Congress, including HB No. 8, HB No. 58 and HB No. 118 (filed June 30, 2025), HB No. 1491, HB No. 1646, HB No. 1927, HB No. 2685, HB No. 3229 and HB No. 3599, all pending in the Committee; their texts were not reviewed.

Similar measures were filed in the 19th Congress (HB No. 127, HB No. 194, HB No. 274, HB No. 1069, HB No. 3300, HB No. 8059, HB No. 8203, SB No. 410 and SB No. 1085) and in the 18th Congress (HB No. 4791, HB No. 7282, HB No. 7680 and HB No. 8850, the last consolidated or substituted in a committee report, and SB No. 2500, which reached Second Reading as a Special Order); their texts were not reviewed.
No substitute bill or committee report on the measure in the 20th Congress is on record.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 11768 seeks to modernize and reorganize the Bureau of Immigration and to consolidate the laws on immigration and alien registration. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 5 (Composition and Qualifications) provides that the Bureau shall be administered by a Board of Commissioners headed by the Commissioner as Chairperson, with two Deputy Commissioners as members, subject to citizenship, age, education and Bar membership requirements.
b. Section 6 (Powers and Functions) provides that the Board shall decide on deportation, visa and legalization of residence cases, exercise contempt powers, issue rules of procedure and publish operations manuals and schedules of fees.
c. Section 11 (Powers and Duties of the Commissioner) provides that the Commissioner shall direct Bureau operations, control personnel, issue mission, commitment and deportation orders, control ports of entry and exit, and adjust or waive fines and penalties.
d. Section 14 (Creation of the Boards of Special Inquiry) and Section 18 (Creation of Positions) provide for up to five Boards of Special Inquiry, each with a Chairperson at Attorney V, Salary Grade 25, and two members at Attorney IV, Salary Grade 23.
e. Section 19 (Divisions and Other Operating Offices of the Bureau) and Section 21 (Organizational Structure and Staffing Pattern of the Bureau) provide for divisions, regional and other operating offices, with the structure and staffing pattern determined by the Board.
f. Section 33 (Powers and Duties) and Section 36 (Border Control Checkpoints) provide for the powers of Immigration Officers, including examination, exclusion and warrantless custody of foreign nationals entering in violation of law, and for border control checkpoints.
g. Sections 37 to 115 provide for the categories of visas and immigrants, quotas, adjustment of status, arrival formalities, exclusion, deportation, alien registration, bonds, fees, fines and penalties.
h. Section 116 (Creation of New Positions, Reclassification of Existing Positions and Upgrading of Salary Levels) provides for the creation, reclassification and upgrading of Bureau positions, including the Commissioner III at Salary Grade 30 and Deputy Commissioner III at Salary Grade 29.
i. Section 117 (Additional Grant of Benefits) provides for night shift differential and overtime pay for Bureau employees.
j. Section 118 (Establishment of Immigration Trust Fund) provides for an Immigration Trust Fund sourced from thirty percent of immigration fees, fines and other income, capped yearly, to be used for modernization, employee benefits and professionalization.
k. Section 119 (Development and Implementation of Electronic Systems) and Section 121 (Reorganization of the Bureau) provide for electronic systems and the reorganization of the Bureau.
l. Section 126 (Appropriations) provides that initial funding shall be charged against the current appropriation of the Bureau of Immigration and thereafter included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
m. Section 128 (Repealing Clause) provides for the repeal of Commonwealth Act No. 613, RA No. 562 and RA No. 750.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 11768 may be considered alongside HB No. 9801, which carries near-identical text, and the other 20th Congress bills on modernizing the Bureau of Immigration. The measure corresponds to item 43 of the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda. The review should assess the cost of the position upgrades and new units under Section 116 (Creation of New Positions, Reclassification of Existing Positions and Upgrading of Salary Levels) and Section 18 (Creation of Positions), the earmarking and non-reversion of collections under Section 118 (Establishment of Immigration Trust Fund), the fiscal effect on LGUs of repealing RA No. 750 under Section 128 (Repealing Clause), and whether the reorganization is consistent with the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231).

Confirm the status of the bill and of the other measures on modernizing the Bureau of Immigration with the House of Representatives, including any consolidation.
